name: q_per_channel_scales
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::q_per_channel_scales(Tensor self) -> Tensor. This signature is representative only; the original Gems pytest calls and results define the full contract, including overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and tests must never be narrowed to this representative signature. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: aten::q_per_channel_scales(Tensor self) -> Tensor; aten::q_per_channel_scales.out(Tensor self, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Semantics: q_per_channel_scales is a quantizer-metadata getter that returns the per-channel scale tensor already held by a per-channel quantized tensor's quantizer, one scale per channel, in float64 for the per_channel_affine family and float32 for the per_channel_affine_float_qparams family. The pytest constructs operands with torch.ops.aten._make_per_channel_quantized_tensor over several per-channel axes and verifies the stored scales against the native reference; the covered inputs include negative-axis metadata and rank-0 inputs. The source only shows that preconstructed negative-axis metadata is accepted and the returned scales match the reference; it does not show this getter resolving, normalizing or computing the axis. The representative default overload returns the quantizer's own internal parameter tensor: that aliasing is internal quantizer storage, not an alias of any tensor argument, so returns_alias_of is empty here. The out overload instead mutates its keyword-only out buffer, filling and returning it and resizing a mismatched buffer; that argument aliasing and mutation belong to aten::q_per_channel_scales.out and are exercised by the original pytest rather than expressed by this representative overload.
